title: Your first component
summary: A component is a class plus a template, marked with the @Component decorator.

quiz.q: What does the `selector` of a component do?
options: Defines the HTML tag used to place the component
quiz.explain: The selector is the custom tag name, for example `app-greeting`, that you write in other templates.

quiz.q: Complete the interpolation that shows the value of `name`.
quiz.explain: Interpolation uses double curly braces: `{{ name }}`.

quiz.q:
A component has `name = 'Meena'` and the template `

Hi {{ name }}

`. What text appears in the heading?
quiz.explain: Angular replaces `{{ name }}` with the value `Meena`.

exercise.task:
Complete `greeting.component.ts`. - Give the component the selector `app-greeting`. - Use the template `

Hello {{ name }}

`. - Add a property `name` set to `'Angular'`.
hints: Everything goes inside the `@Component({ ... })` settings and the class body.
Add `selector: 'app-greeting'` and `template: ...` to the settings. In the class write `name = 'Angular';`.

checks.name: It uses the @Component decorator
checks.hint: Keep the @Component decorator above the class.

checks.name: The template shows Hello {{ name }} in an h1
The class has name set to 'Angular'
